desc: decimal must be exact base-10 arithmetic — 0.1 + 0.2 == 0.3 holds exactly (doc's explicit worked claim); no float drift. Runtime-value assertion, not just a compile-accept.
exercise: field A as decimal default 0.1; field B as decimal default 0.2; rule A + B == 0.3 because "decimal is exact"

desc: number is IEEE 754 double — 0.1 + 0.2 != 0.3 (doc's explicit worked claim). The rule compiles (line 83: 'proof engine cannot prove exact equality on number', so it is not statically rejected); the drift is a runtime-observable value, which Phase 2 must check against the doc's claim rather than treat as a bare compile-accept.
exercise: field A as number default 0.1; field B as number default 0.2; rule A + B == 0.3 because "number is approximate"
